If Procurement requires competition, propose a lightweight RFQ (2–3 vendors) or use the approved-vendor framework as a faster alternative to a full RFP, and document all approvals.

rounds.response: Short answer: your internal comparison can support a sole-source request only if it clearly documents why no reasonable alternative meets the scope (e.g., unique analytics, required integrations, data-residency or security constraints, or disproportionate transition costs) and includes market research showing other vendors don’t match — otherwise Procurement will typically ask for at least 1–2 additional quotes. Prepare a concise sole-source justification that states the non-duplicable requirements, shows the market scan, quantifies TCO (including LearnFast exit costs), and attaches Security/Legal signoffs, then ask Procurement to confirm acceptance. If you want to avoid the risk of rejection, run a short RFQ to two comparable vendors (target three quotes total) with a tight deadline (5–7 business days) to minimize delay. I can draft the sole-source memo or a 3-vendor RFQ template — tell me which and share the expected annual spend plus two alternative vendor names if you have them.
